en: The guests came to grandfather's milestone birthday.
note: A person's ю́билей is a round-numbered birthday. "Jubilee" is not what English calls it and "anniversary" asks "anniversary of what?" — neither of the earlier renderings was ordinary English.
en_alt: The guests came to grandfather's birthday celebration.

en: We are celebrating grandmother's milestone birthday.
note: Same: an anniversary in English belongs to an event, and a jubilee to an institution or a reign.
en_alt: We are celebrating grandmother's big birthday.

note: The rewrite added a claim the Russian does not make. Russian masculine plural вну́ки covers a mixed group, so "grandsons" asserts they are all male.

en: The professor devoted the lecture to difficult problems.
note: The rewrite narrowed the Russian to match the headword hint; the sentence does not commit to that reading. зада́ча is a problem as readily as a task, and a lecture is devoted to problems.
en_alt: The professor devoted the lecture to complex tasks.

en: The classics never go out of date.
note: The rewrite narrowed the Russian to match the headword hint; the sentence does not commit to that reading. Кла́ссика covers classic works of any art; nothing here says music.
en_alt: Classical music never goes out of date.

en: There are various lids in the drawer.
note: The rewrite narrowed the Russian to match the headword hint; the sentence does not commit to that reading. я́щик is a drawer or a box and the sentence chooses neither.
en_alt: There are various lids in the box.

ru: Он снял пиджа́к и сел за стол.
en: He took off his jacket and sat down at the table.
note: The rewrite narrowed the Russian to match the headword hint; the sentence does not commit to that reading. A пиджа́к is the jacket of a suit; "blazer" is one particular kind of jacket.
en_alt: He took off his blazer and sat down at the table.

en: The shop assistant helped me choose a present.
note: The hint's wording is not what an English speaker says here; the sentence was fine. "Shop assistant" is the British English term this corpus is written in.
en_alt: The salesperson helped me choose a present.

en: All the relatives came for the holiday.
note: The hint's wording is not what an English speaker says here; the sentence was fine. "Kin" is archaic; родня́ is the everyday word for one's relatives.

ru: Она́ извини́ла бы его́, е́сли бы он попроси́л.
en: She would forgive him if he asked.
note: The rewrite narrowed the Russian to match the headword hint; the sentence does not commit to that reading. "Excuse him" reads as excusing his absence; forgiving is the likely sense of извини́ть here.
en_alt: She would excuse him if he asked.
